t.1.36.1: Long ago, while the god was performing austerities, the gods together with the hosts of seers, desiring a commander for their army, approached the Grandsire.
t.1.36.2: Then all the gods, together with Indra and led by Agni, bowed down before the blessed Grandsire and spoke these auspicious words.
t.1.36.3: O god, he who was formerly given to us by the Blessed One as our commander has undertaken the supreme austerity and is practising penance together with Umā.
t.1.36.5: Having heard the words of the deities, the Grandfather of all the worlds, consoling the gods with sweet words, spoke this to them.
t.1.36.4: Whatever must be done next in this matter, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds, arrange it, O knower of ordinances, for you are indeed our supreme refuge.
t.1.36.6: What was spoken by the mountain's daughter, that you shall have no offspring in your wives, that word of hers is unfailing and true indeed; there is no doubt.
t.1.36.7: This is Gaṅgā, who flows through the sky, in whom the Fire-god will beget a son, the enemy-subduing commander of the army of the gods.
t.1.36.8: The eldest daughter of the lord of mountains will honour that son; this will be greatly esteemed by Umā, there is no doubt.
t.1.36.9: Having heard those words of his, O Raghunandana, all the gods, their purpose fulfilled, bowed down and worshipped the Grandfather.
t.1.36.10: O Rāma, all the deities went to Mount Kailāsa, adorned with minerals, and there they appointed Agni for the purpose of obtaining a son.
t.1.36.11: O god, O Hutāśana, accomplish this task of the gods; O greatly radiant one, release the seed-energy into Gaṅgā, the daughter of the mountain.
t.1.36.12: Having given his promise to the gods, Pāvaka approached Gaṅgā and said: "O goddess, bear this embryo; this is pleasing to the gods."
t.1.36.13: Hearing these words, she assumed a divine form; and he, beholding her majesty, scattered it over her on every side.
t.1.36.14: Then Pāvaka sprinkled the goddess on every side, and all the streams of Gaṅgā were filled, O Raghunandana.
t.1.36.15: Then Gaṅgā said to him, the priest of all the gods: "O god, I am unable to hold this surging energy of yours; burning with that fire, my mind is deeply distressed."
t.1.36.16: Then Hutāśana, the fire of all the gods, said this to Gaṅgā: "Here, at the foot of the Himālaya, let this embryo be deposited."
t.1.36.17: Having heard Agni's words, O sinless one, the mighty and radiant Gaṅgā then released that exceedingly brilliant embryo from her streams.
t.1.36.18: That which issued from her, shining like refined Jāmbūnada gold, reached the earth, and from it came gold, pure and lovely.
t.1.36.19: From its sharpness there arose copper and black iron, and its dross there became tin and lead.
t.1.36.20: Having reached the earth, that very seed grew and became minerals of many kinds.
t.1.36.21: No sooner had the embryo been laid down than the entire forest clothing the mountain, suffused with its radiance, turned to gold.
t.1.36.22: From that time onward, O Rāghava, tiger among men, gold, whose radiance equals that of the fire, has been known as jātarūpa.
t.1.36.23: Then the gods, together with Indra and accompanied by the hosts of Maruts, engaged the Kṛttikās to nourish with milk that boy who had been born.
t.1.36.24: Having made an excellent compact, they gave milk to the newborn child, resolved in their minds: "This is the son of us all."
t.1.36.25: Then all the deities, speaking the name Kārttikeya, declared: “This son will be renowned throughout the three worlds; of that there is no doubt.”
t.1.36.26: Having heard those words of theirs, they bathed the child who had slipped forth in the flow from the womb, shining with supreme splendor like a blazing fire.
t.1.36.27: O Kākutstha, the gods called the illustrious Kārttikeya, radiant like fire, 'Skanda,' because he had issued forth in the outflow of the embryo.
t.1.36.28: Then the most excellent milk appeared in the six Kṛttikās, and, becoming six-faced, he drank the milk flowing from their breasts.
t.1.36.30: Then the hosts of gods, led by Agni, assembled together and consecrated him of spotless splendour as the commander of the armies of the gods.
t.1.36.29: Having taken the milk, the mighty lord, still tender of body, then conquered the hosts of the Daitya armies by his own valor within a single day.
t.1.36.31: O Rāma, I have told you this detailed account of Gaṅgā, and also the birth of Kumāra, which is blessed and holy as well.
